description: MAIN-PARA's EIBCALEN = 0 guard at app/cbl/COADM01C.cbl:82-84 - the transaction typed at a clear screen, with no communication area at all. The program moves 'COSGN00C' into CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM (line 83 sets FROM, not TO - the asymmetry with line 97 is in the source and is reproduced) and performs RETURN-TO-SIGNON-SCREEN, whose combined relation at line 162 then finds CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM naming nothing and defaults it to 'COSGN00C' as well. No map is sent, so sends is empty and the response IS the whole observable behaviour, which is why it is stated field by field; the single line the run emits is the 78-byte ERRMSGO that line 80 blanked, declared on the SCREEN_ERRMSG_78 channel because the 80-byte WS-MESSAGE of line 38 is working storage and only a controller produces the screen field it narrows into. The XCTL at lines 165-167 specifies NO COMMAREA, unlike the one at 142-145. EIBAID is never read on this path - line 93 is not reached - so no AID is declared: naming one would suggest the key mattered. Driven through the controller because an absent request body is how GET /api/admin/menu expresses EIBCALEN = 0, and the invocation is declared in screenRequest because that is where ParityCase requires an online request to live: jobParameters models a JCL PARM and is refused for any unit kind other than BATCH_JOB. Gate G38 asks for both the ENTER and the REENTER path of an online program, and this case is neither - it is the earliest of MAIN-PARA's three arms, the one line 82 takes before either of the others is reachable. The ENTER half of that pair is case02 at lines 87-90 and the REENTER half is the EVALUATE EIBAID at 93-103, which case09, case10 and case11 drive arm by arm. Nothing is highlighted here and nothing may be: G38 is usually phrased around the DFHRED-and-asterisk highlight CSSETATY applies, but COADM01C does not copy CSSETATY - its COPY list at lines 50-61 is COCOM01Y, COADM02Y, COADM01, COTTL01Y, CSDAT01Y, CSMSG01Y, CSUSR01Y, DFHAID and DFHBMSCA - and DFHRED appears nowhere in its 268 lines. Red reaches the screen only as ERRMSG's declared COLOR at app/bms/COADM01.bms:154-157, and the one attribute byte the program ever writes is the DFHGREEN of line 148, on the coming-soon path this case never reaches; expecting a highlight or an asterisk would be inventing behaviour. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:32, the timestamp COADM01C's own version footer at line 267 carries, so the instant is anchored in the source rather than chosen, and all twenty cases in this directory pin that same instant and name US-ASCII explicitly rather than leaving a code page to a platform default. This path performs no POPULATE-HEADER-INFO, so it paints no header and the instant changes nothing it asserts; it is declared all the same, so that one clock governs the whole directory and no two cases can differ by their clock. Every expected value above is statically derived - read out of the COBOL paragraph that produces it and cross-checked against the 160-byte layout of app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy, the xxxI PICTURE clauses of app/cpy-bms/COADM01.CPY and the DFHMDF definitions of app/bms/COADM01.bms - and none of it was captured from an execution of the legacy program, which is empirically impossible here: no z/OS or CICS runtime, an indexed file handler the available compiler reports as disabled, no Language Environment CEE services, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR absent from the repository. ParityCase's own class documentation is the authoritative statement of that provenance, and the substitution is escalated rather than absorbed (risk R-A).
